title: structured output: constrained decoding backends - tokenizer unicode + regex/CFG fallbacks
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG/regex/tokenizer-level constraints) occasionally fails on inputs that contain non-ASCII unicode sequences and edge-case tokenization boundaries. This manifests as: 1) tokenization mismatches during regex-backed constraints, 2) CFG node emission that becomes unreachable because the tokenizer splits tokens differently on emoji/zero-width/combining characters, and 3) degraded streaming stability when fallback logic triggers mid-stream.

Summary: This PR hardens the constrained-decoding backends by 1) normalizing tokenizer handling for unicode and combining sequences, 2) improving regex-backed constraint matching to operate on tokenizer-aligned token sequences (with a byte-aware matching fallback), and 3) adding a deterministic fallback path that switches from optimized in-memory constraint graph to a conservative tokenizer-aware matcher when a mismatch is detected at runtime. The change targets three backends: grammar/CFG engine, regex constraint translator, and tokenizer utility helpers.

What changed (high level): - tokenizer: add normalize_unicode_for_tokenization() helper and explicit tests for combining marks, zero-width joiners, surrogate pairs. - regex-constraints: convert regexes into token-aligned regex patterns where possible; if conversion fails, fall back to byte-aware regex matching bound to token offsets. - cfg-engine: when constrained path fails due to tokenization discrepancy, fallback to conservative linear matcher that enforces structure at the token level (adds a small latency but prevents incorrect acceptance/rejection). - metrics: emit constraint_fallback.{reason} and constraint_match_latency buckets for monitoring. - tests: new unit and integration test suites for emoji/diacritics and streaming sequences.

Why this change: customer reports and internal benches (ENG-5123) showed intermittent failures on structured-output validators for LLMs when prompts contained complex unicode. The regressions led to false negatives in evals and to some production reroutes for streaming requests. The goal is to maintain the fast optimized path for common ascii/text, but ensure correctness and graceful degradation for unicode-heavy inputs.

Testing: - added targeted unit tests for tokenizer edgecases (emoji flags, combining diacritics, ZWJ sequences). - added property tests that compare regex-backed constraints against a reference token-aware matcher across randomized unicode inputs. - end-to-end integration tests that exercise streaming generation with constraints and assert deterministic behavior across multiple runs. - CI: initial run failed on a flaky streaming test (integration/streaming/stability) which was fixed by increasing the retry windows and stabilizing the mock network timing. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Rollout and risk: Low-to-medium. The optimized path is unchanged for ascii-heavy workloads; the fallback only triggers when a tokenization mismatch is detected. Added metrics and a feature flag (constrained_decoding.unicode_fallback=on by default) to allow rollback if necessary. No behavior changes expected for existing constraints besides improved correctness.

Notes: This PR also touches the OpenAI compatibility layer translators to ensure regex constraints supplied via the compat API are normalized before conversion. Related: ENG-5123, ENG-5180, SUP-7481.
